entries.title: Create and Writing Copilot hide job title and company from users without contact access
entries.summary: Team members whose event role does not grant access to contacts, speakers, exhibitors, sponsors or accounts no longer see participant job titles or company names in **Redraft** output or **Writing Copilot** responses. Names and session roles are still included; only the protected details are withheld. Org admins and roles with contact access continue to receive full attribution.
entries.use_case: Organisations that restrict certain team members (for example, a marketing role with no people access) from viewing contact details can now be confident that Create and the Writing Copilot will not inadvertently expose job titles or company names to those users through generated content.

cs_action.note: Behaviour change is automatic; no configuration required. Restricted users will notice that Redraft and Copilot responses no longer include job titles or company names for participants.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about data privacy for team members who should not see speaker or contact details, or when a customer has roles scoped to marketing-only access.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with event team roles that have partial contact permissions — common in larger organisations with separate marketing and programme teams.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Create → Redraft or Writing Copilot
internal.gotchas: Drafts already saved by a user who previously had contact access keep their existing text and citation chips; the gate applies only to new drafts, redrafts and Copilot turns going forward.
internal.talk_track: If a team member's role can't read contacts, Create now respects that boundary — they'll see speaker names and session roles in generated content, but not job titles or company names.

entries.title: Credit type details save correctly for common increment values
entries.summary: **Save details** on a credit type's **Details** tab now works for all valid increment values. Previously, common values such as 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 triggered a browser step-mismatch error that silently blocked the save request from being sent.
entries.use_case: Organizers setting up credit types with standard increment values (0.25, 0.5, 1, etc.) can now save changes to the Details tab without the form silently failing.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that saving credit type details appears to do nothing, or that changes to the Accreditor or other fields are not persisting.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Credit Claiming with credit types that have increments like 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 or 1.
internal.gotchas: The bug only affected the Details tab save; the designation panel (SessionCreditDesignationPanel) was unaffected.
internal.talk_track: A browser validation bug was silently blocking saves on the credit type Details tab for the most common increment values — that is now fixed.

entries.title: Sponsor and exhibitor contact roles are now visible and editable on the group profile
entries.summary: Each contact listed on a sponsor or exhibitor group profile now shows their role as a badge. The row menu includes **Edit role**, which opens a dialog with the default roles and any roles already in use as suggestions; leaving the field empty clears the role. The same badge and edit option appear in the **Sponsor/Exhibitor Profile** sidebar.
entries.use_case: Organizers who collect contact roles through the sponsor or exhibitor intake form can now see those roles at a glance on the group profile and correct or clear them without leaving the page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why roles collected on the intake form were not visible to admins, or wants to manage sponsor/exhibitor contact roles after submission.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using sponsor or exhibitor intake forms with the contact-role question.
internal.staff_path: Sponsors or Exhibitors → open a group → Contacts tab → row menu → Edit role
internal.gotchas: Roles are saved through the existing PUT /account/:id/contact-relationships endpoint; no new API surface. Requires the matching web-api PR on the same branch.
internal.talk_track: Roles your sponsors filled in on the intake form now show as badges on their profile, and you can edit or clear any role directly from the contacts list.

entries.title: Dispatch: Slack shows as connected and delivers DMs to team members by email when no Slack ID is found
entries.summary: The **Dispatch** editor no longer incorrectly shows "Slack isn't connected" when the Slack roster fails to load — the connection status stays accurate. Team members who have no Slack user ID now receive a direct message looked up by email address automatically; if no match is found, they fall back to email delivery only.
entries.use_case: Teams using Dispatch with Slack were seeing a false "Slack isn't connected" warning and missing DMs to teammates whose Slack IDs weren't stored — both issues are now resolved so every send reaches the right people.

cs_action.note: Default-on fix; no action needed. Affected customers may have already noticed the false warning or missing DMs.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that Dispatch says Slack is not connected even though Apps → Slack shows it is, or that team members are not receiving Slack DMs from a Dispatch send.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Dispatch with Slack enabled.
internal.gotchas: Team members with no Slack ID and no matching email in the Slack workspace will still fall back to email-only delivery.
internal.talk_track: Dispatch now correctly reads the Slack connection status even when the roster is slow to load, and it looks up teammates by email when their Slack ID isn't on file — so DMs go out reliably.

entries.title: Report exports use the correct sheet name, shared pivot reports match the builder, and contact-profile access is enforced by role
entries.summary: Four user-visible fixes shipped together. **Exported reports** now name the Excel sheet after the report (e.g. "Session Summary") instead of the generic label "Report". **Shared saved reports** that include a pivot now return the same pivoted row count as the report builder, rather than the raw unpivoted rows. **Contact profile** pages at the organization level now require the viewer to be an org member with org access, or to hold a role on one of the org's events that can view Contacts, Speakers, Exhibitors, Sponsors or Accounts — event-only staff (such as Evaluators) who previously slipped through are now correctly denied. A security fix also ensures that **SbQL queries run under impersonation** use the target user's record scope, so contact-rule limits and session-scope restrictions are applied correctly. **Insights** now needs **Can view reports** for event-only team members, and report links from a scheduled report keep the saved pivot.
entries.use_case: Organizers who download reports to Excel no longer have to rename the sheet before sharing. Teams using shared pivot reports can trust that the link delivers the same summarised data they see in the builder. Admins can be confident that event-only staff (e.g. Evaluators) cannot read contact profiles they have no permission to see.

cs_action.note: All four fixes are default-on bug fixes; no action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their exported Excel sheet is always named 'Report', that a shared pivot link shows more rows than the builder, or that an Evaluator-role user can open contact profiles they should not see.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using report exports, shared saved reports with pivots, or event-only staff roles.
internal.staff_path: Insights → Reports → Download (for sheet name); share a saved pivot report link (for pivot fix); Contacts profile page (for access fix)
internal.gotchas: Event-only staff with has_org_access = false (e.g. Evaluators, custom roles with People off) will now receive a 403 on org-level contact profile pages they could previously open. ~2,500 users on prod are affected. Confirm with the customer that this is the intended behaviour before escalating.
internal.talk_track: We fixed three report accuracy issues and tightened contact-profile access so only people with the right event role can open a contact's org-level profile.

entries.title: All Off / All On buttons now appear only on the Permissions tab and ask for confirmation
entries.summary: The **All Off** and **All On** buttons in the role editor now appear only on the **Permissions** tab, not on the **Fields**, **Statuses** or **Notifications** tabs. Both buttons show a confirmation prompt before applying the change. This prevents accidentally wiping or granting every permission while working on unrelated role settings. The fix applies to both event roles and organization roles.
entries.use_case: Prevents a team admin from accidentally resetting all permissions on a role (such as Co-Chair) while editing its field visibility or notification settings — a mistake that previously wiped carefully configured access without warning.

cs_action.note: Default-on bug fix; no action needed. Relevant if a customer reports that a role's permissions were wiped — this fix prevents recurrence.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that a role lost all its permissions unexpectedly, or asks whether bulk-toggle is safe to use.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who manages custom roles with fine-grained permissions, especially those with Co-Chair or vendor roles.
internal.gotchas: ILTA had a Co-Chair role wiped by this bug before the fix. If a customer reports a similar incident, the fix is now live and a confirmation prompt guards future changes.
internal.talk_track: All Off and All On now only appear on the Permissions tab and ask you to confirm before applying, so there is no risk of accidentally clearing a role while adjusting field or notification settings.

entries.title: Review plan fixes: AI persona exports, closed-allocation visibility, multi-file fields, plan monitor speed, and reviewer thread notifications
entries.summary: Five fixes to review plans ship together. **Grade**, **Score Summary** and **Cumulative** exports now include submissions assigned to AI personas (previously dropped). Submissions whose allocations were all closed by a per-reviewer limit now appear in the **Plan Monitor** as **Closed: x of N** instead of disappearing. Multi-file submission fields show all uploaded files to reviewers in the portal (previously only the first file). The **Plan Monitor** page loads significantly faster on large plans. Reviewers who participated in an earlier round no longer receive email notifications for messages posted in later rounds they are not assigned to.
entries.use_case: Organizers running AI-assisted reviews can now export complete grade and score data without missing persona-assigned submissions, and reviewers in the portal see all files attached to a submission rather than just the first one.

cs_action.note: All five fixes are default-on bug fixes; no action required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports missing rows in review exports, a submission disappearing from the plan monitor when review limits are in use, reviewers seeing only one file when multiple were uploaded, slow plan monitor page loads on large events, or reviewers from ended rounds getting emailed about new messages.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using v2 review plans, especially those using AI Screener personas, per-reviewer review limits, multi-file submission fields, large plans, or multi-round reviewer threads.
internal.gotchas: The multi-file fix returns an array for multi-file fields; single-file fields keep the existing single-object shape the portal already reads. The notification fix only drops reviewer participants whose live v2 assignments are all in rounds past their end date; v1/org plans and @mentions are unaffected.
internal.talk_track: Wave 4 of the review sweep closes five QA-bounced issues: complete exports when AI personas are used, correct monitor counts under review limits, all files visible to reviewers, faster monitor page loads, and quieter email notifications for reviewers whose rounds have ended.

entries.title: Portal session dates now follow the portal's language and date-style setting
entries.summary: Session date labels throughout the speaker portal — on the home page, **My Participation**, task group headers and the session detail view — now respect the portal's **Language** setting and the event's **Record Settings** date style. German portals show dates in German order (e.g. "Do., 22. Apr., 10:15 - 11:00 CEST"); English portals on events configured with a European date style show day-before-month order (e.g. "Mon 19 Oct, 14:00") instead of US order.

where.path: Portals → [portal name] → (home, My Participation, task groups, session detail)

entries.use_case: Events running non-English portals or using a European date format no longer show speakers dates in the wrong locale order — German speakers see German-formatted dates, and EU-style English events show day-before-month throughout the portal.

cs_action.note: English portals on events where Record Settings has advocacy_datetime_format = 'eu', or where no date style is set on a 24-hour event, will change from US-style ('Mon, Oct 19th, 14:00') to EU-style ('Mon 19 Oct, 14:00') automatically. Heads-up for any customer who has screenshotted or documented their portal date format.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that portal dates are in the wrong language or wrong day/month order, or when onboarding a non-US event that uses a European date style.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running a non-English portal or an English portal on an event configured with a European date style.
internal.staff_path: Event → Record Settings → date style; Portal → Language setting
internal.gotchas: English portals on 24-hour events with no explicit date style set will silently switch to EU order (day before month). This is the correct behaviour but may surprise customers who were used to the old US default.
internal.talk_track: Dates in the portal now match the language and date style you've already configured — no extra setup needed.

entries.title: Swoogo sync summary shows Registration ID counts and unmatched or ambiguous registrants
entries.summary: The Swoogo sync summary now has a **Swoogo Registration IDs** section with the counts written, and warnings for registrants that matched no contact or matched more than one. Leaving **Version** empty in **Event Settings** no longer breaks every sync.
entries.use_case: Organizers who write Swoogo Registration IDs back to contacts can see exactly which registrants were skipped and why.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why some Swoogo registrants have no Registration ID on their contact.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Swoogo and write-back on.
internal.gotchas: Registrants only match on email address; the summary lists the ones that did not. Needs Swoogo registrants whose emails match contacts to show counts.
internal.talk_track: The sync now tells you which registrants it could not match, instead of leaving you to guess.

entries.title: Email Campaigns: Add unsubscribe works and shows what went wrong
entries.summary: **Add unsubscribe** on **Settings → Unsubscribes** now saves the contact you add, and the dialog shows the reason when it cannot.

where.path: Communications → Email Campaigns → Settings → Unsubscribes → Add unsubscribe

entries.use_case: Organizers can honor an opt-out they received by email or phone straight away.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports Add unsubscribe doing nothing.
internal.staff_path: Communications → Email Campaigns → Settings → Unsubscribes → Add unsubscribe
internal.gotchas: The button failed silently before; no data was lost.
internal.talk_track: You can add an unsubscribe by hand again, and you see the error if it fails.

entries.title: Speakers you hide no longer appear on share cards or in Dispatch
entries.summary: A speaker hidden from the public listing in the session editor or run of show is now also left off **share cards**, **Dispatch** posts and embeds.

where.path: Program → Sessions → session → hide speaker (eye icon)

entries.use_case: Organizers can hide a speaker once and trust every public surface to respect it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer saw a hidden speaker on a share card or Dispatch post.
internal.staff_path: Program → Sessions → session → hide speaker (eye icon)
internal.gotchas: Rows hidden before the fix are corrected by a one-time data update that Josh runs; until then a few older sessions may still show.
internal.talk_track: Hide a speaker once and it holds everywhere.

entries.title: Media upload, playback and download work for EU events
entries.summary: Uploading, playing back and downloading media, including thumbnails, transcripts, podcast audio and clip downloads, now works for events in the EU.
entries.use_case: Organizers with EU events can upload and use recordings and files like everyone else.

internal.when_to_bring_up: An EU customer could not upload or play media.
internal.gotchas: No setting involved. Do not describe storage regions to customers.
internal.talk_track: Media now works end to end for EU events.

entries.title: Insights and Report Builder include AI persona reviews
entries.summary: Review data in **Insights** and **Report Builder** now includes reviews by AI personas, named after the persona.
entries.use_case: Review reports and Insights answers match what the plan monitor and exports already show.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer notices persona reviews missing from a review report.
internal.gotchas: Before this, only reviews by people appeared in Insights and Report Builder.
internal.talk_track: Persona reviews now show up in reports under the persona name.

entries.title: Portal subsession panel shows and edits Tags, Language, Track and Level
entries.summary: The subsession panel in the speaker portal now shows and edits **Tags**, **Language**, **Track** and **Level** when the portal shows those fields.
entries.use_case: Submitters can see and fix a subsession's classification from the portal.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says subsession tags are missing in the portal.
internal.gotchas: Only shown when the portal's session field configuration includes the field.
internal.talk_track: Subsessions now carry their tags, language, track and level in the portal.
